results.reason: Issue 3 contrasts Schedule §1.1 (shipment from Verdane's plant) with MSA §1.3 (delivery at Rochester). It explains that late-delivery remedies (§5.2), risk of loss (§5.3/Sched §5.1) and the invoice/payment trigger now key off shipment, shifting transit delay and risk to Harlow.
The fix adds an order-of-precedence clause making the MSA control. It also revises or deletes Schedule §1.1 so Delivery Date means delivery at the Ship-To Location, in line with the MSA definition.

Issue 1 identifies that MSA §4.3 covers all housings and similar components worldwide, against the Term Sheet's Series 7/US limit. It explains this captures non-Series 7 parts and any foreign purchasing, and recommends narrowing to Series 7 Housings for US delivery.

Issue 5 identifies that Verdane may assign to any person without consent while Harlow needs consent. It explains the risk of an unknown, weaker or competing assignee receiving Harlow's confidential drawings. It recommends requiring Harlow's prior written consent and a termination right on change of control or assignment to a competitor.

Issue 2 explains that Amendment §§2.1–2.2 strip gross negligence and the IP indemnity from the §11.2 exclusions and subject them to the §11.1 cap. It recommends restoring the original exclusions and not signing the Amendment in that form.
The memo states the cap is fees paid in the prior 12 months (§11.1). It also states the original §11.2 excluded gross negligence, willful misconduct and the IP Indemnity.
The memo states that Term Sheet §3.1 limits exclusivity to Series 7 Housings within the United States and uses this as the baseline for comparing MSA §4.3.

The memo states New York law governs per MSA §16.1 and frames its enforceability points under NY principles. It includes an assumptions and facts-needed section. It cites no cases; the one statutory reference (UCC 2-305) is accurate and is flagged as needing confirmation.

The memo is structured as a partner memo with a bottom line and issues ordered by importance. Each issue has Where, Why it matters and Fix, and there is a dedicated Assumptions and facts needed section.
The Term Sheet is used as the deal baseline and a negotiating point. Execution status is noted only as a fact to confirm, and the 3-year term and 45-day payment terms are not treated as defects.

Exclusivity is correctly attributed to MSA §4.3 and assignment to §15.2, with the correct party benefiting in each case. No cases are cited, and the UCC reference is flagged for verification in Section 4.
